text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

United States telecommunications giant Bell South came close to liquidating Optus Communications last week during negotiations with its fellow shareholders. Bell declared the Optus Vision arm of the business should be wound up, but local shareholder Mayne Nickless said that if Bell moved on Optus Vision, it would put its own liquidator into the whole company. Page 1.

Some fund managers are concerned over the book-building process used for large stock offers such as the bidding process for shares in ICI Australia Ltd. One fund manager suggested the Australian Securities Commission or the Australian Stock Exchange shoud look at the process to see if it was fair. Page 39.

Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd has spread into Indonesia, several areas of Europe and the Philippines in its bid to build up its multi-billion dollar fizzy drink empire, but is unable to capture just 1.25 per cent of the Australian market in the Northern Territory. This area is current held by Queensland-based dairy company QUF Industries Ltd. Page 39.

News of the record A$876 million tax bill against Industrial Equity Ltd saw shares in Tooth & Co Ltd fall 32 per cent yesterday, and may lead to a downgrading in value for other members of the once strong Adsteam group. Analysts say Tooth was worst affected because it is the only one of the three members viewed as having any hope of ending up with surplus cash after the group paid off its debts. Page 39.

Following its buyout of Australian Newsprint Mills from News Limited , New Zealand-based Fletcher Challenge Ltd chief executive officer Hugh Fletcher said the company will review its Australian paper production and mill design options with a possible second newsprint mill at Albury and work on its Boyer Mill in Tasmania being looked at. Page 40.

Australian construction and engineering company Transfield has teamed up with British water company Anglian Water International to bid for water and waste water treatment projects in New South Wales, Victoria and Queensland. The two companies may also bid for projects in Asia, with a project in Indonesia currently being negotiated. Page 43.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australia's gold industry and the West Australian Government have attacked the Reserve Bank's surprise announcement that it has sold most of Australia's bullion reserves. West Australian Resources Minister Colin Barnett said his Government had not been consulted in the decision, which would send a "very odd signal" to the gold market. Page 21.

Adelaide-based retailer Harris Scarfe has for most of its 147 years languished around the bottom of the department store ladder, but with leading retailer David Jones battling an identity crisis and Myer Grace Bros moving into David Jones' territory, Harrs Scarfe has pushed itself into the big league. Page 21.

Figures released by the Department of Transport for January indicate the previously booming domestic air travel market in Australia may now be shrinking, adding to the woes of Australia's domestic airlines Ansett and Qantas. The figures showed a two per cent drop for domestic paying passengers in January of last year. Page 21.

Coles Myer shares rose to a record close of A$7.04 yesterday as ratings agency Standard & Poors forecast continued market share growth for both Coles and Woolworths. However the S&P forecast, in its Credit-Focus, paints an unpromising picture for Davids and Foodland Associated, which supply to smaller and independent groups, who have been losing market share to the larger companies. Page 23.

Speaking at an Asialink lunch at Melbourne yesterday, National Australia Bank chief executive Don Argus said the bank is looking at potential investments in Asia which would draw on its key strengths such as mortgages and credit cards. While not being spcific, Argus hinted at several "joint ventures, alliances and acquisitions." Page 23.

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission deputy chair Allan Asher told the South Australian Government yesterday its Cooper Basin gas field legislation is contrary to a Council of Australian Governments gas reform agreement. Asher said a failure by State governments to embrace competition could lead to a break down in the national gas reform process. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The gold market is under further pressure following the Reserve Bank's announcement that 167 tonnes of its reserve has been sold. Gold closed locally at a 51-week low of US$332 an ounce this week, which led to the Gold index falling to its lowest level snce 1993. Page 25.

Optus Communications is talking tough with Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation over the bid for a peace deal in rugby league. Optus says Super League is the stumbling block in negotiations over a shake up of Australia's pay-TV industry, and it is determine to be a main player in the talks. Page 25.

Brambles shares, which have jumped about 35 per cent over the past two months, have risen further to a record A$27 following speculation it will form an alliance with GE Capital Services to develop a plastic pallet pool in the United States. Page 25.

United Kingdom retail giant Marks and Spencer, which opens in Australia next year, is negotiating with Qantas for the airline's catering operations. The move could be a healthy spin-off for the airline, which is already supplying lines to Woolworths in Ne South Wales and its subsidiary Safeway in Victoria. Page 25.

The latest issue of Australian Accountant, the monthly publication of the Australian Society of Certified Practising Accountants, has assessed the Howard Government's progress on tax and deregulation issues as a satisfactory C+. The rating follows widespead concern about the Government's commitment to reform. Page 27.

The National Australia Bank's latest Quarterly Business Survey says official interest rates will probably be cut again during July before increasing moderately next year. The survey also showed dropping profits in the mining, manufacturing, and wholesale sectors, raising concerns about the Federal Government's ability to reach its economic predictions. Page 27.
THE AGE

A Reserve Bank official said last night the Bank was severely constrained in the timing of its huge gold sell-off, and was unable to sell the gold earlier to fetch a price of around US$400 an ounce. Instead, the Bank achieved prices as high at US$350 an unce, a price the Bank defended by comparing it to the current price of US$332.40 an ounce. Page B1.

Following in the footsteps of the other major banks the Commonwealth Bank, which has the largest retail customer base in Australia, will today launch a new loyalty program for its credit card customers offering Qantas frequent flyer points and rebates on ank fees. Page B1.

Aussie Home Loans announced yesterday it has boosted its home-lending levels by 45 per cent after writing A$3.26 billion of home loans and refinancing in the 12 months to 30 June. Because of this result, the lender expects to record a pre-tax profit of A$5 million for the 1997 financial year. Page B3.

Fortis Australia, acting for the Motor Trades Association of Australia Superannuation Fund, has bought the Camberwell Safeway and Target retail complex for A$28.14 million on an eight per cent yield. The property was redeveloped in 1995 after it was bougt by Woolworths for A$12.9 million. Page B3.

In a statement yesterday the Speedrail Group, one of the six consortia short-listed by the New South Wales Government to prepare a detailed proposal for the Very High Speed Train service between Sydney and Canberra, said its service for the project would perate from the St James railway station in Sydney to the Canberra Airport. Page B4.

The membership base of personal services company CUC will double following its announcement that it has bought the business assets of loyalty marketing outfit Presidential Card, which markets entertainment, travel and discount cards across Australia and New Zealand. Page B4.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
